cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: AAA rupture red flags
cards.answer: Classic triad: (1) Hypotension (2) Pulsatile abdominal mass (3) Abdominal/back/flank pain → IMMEDIATE vascular surgery, NO CT if unstable

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Mesenteric ischemia red flag
cards.answer: Severe pain out of proportion to examination + elderly + AF → URGENT CT angiogram, IMMEDIATE surgery consult

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Ectopic pregnancy red flag
cards.answer: Woman of childbearing age (15-50) with abdominal pain + amenorrhea + PV bleeding → ALWAYS do βhCG

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: DKA ICU referral criteria
cards.answer: pH <7.1, GCS <12, K+ <3.0 despite replacement, Pregnancy, Age <18 years, Hypotension

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Ascending cholangitis
cards.answer: Charcot's triad (RUQ pain + fever + jaundice) → URGENT resuscitation, antibiotics, ERCP within 24-48h

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Perforated viscus
cards.answer: Sudden severe abdominal pain + peritonism (guarding, rigidity, rebound) + air under diaphragm → IMMEDIATE surgery

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Tension pneumothorax
cards.answer: Tracheal deviation away from affected side + hypotension + respiratory distress → IMMEDIATE needle decompression

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Subarachnoid hemorrhage red flag
cards.answer: Sudden thunderclap headache (worst headache of life) + meningism → URGENT CT head + LP if CT negative

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Temporal arteritis red flag
cards.answer: Age >50 + new headache + jaw claudication + visual symptoms → URGENT ESR/CRP + start prednisolone BEFORE biopsy

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
cards.answer: Severe eye pain + blurred vision + halos around lights + fixed mid-dilated pupil → URGENT ophthalmology

cards.question: Differential: s: RUQ pain differentials
cards.answer:
• Biliary colic
• Acute cholecystitis
• Ascending cholangitis
• Hepatitis
• Pyelonephritis (right)
• Pneumonia (RLL)

cards.question: Differential: s: Epigastric pain differentials
cards.answer:
• Peptic ulcer disease
• GORD
• Acute pancreatitis
• Perforated ulcer
• AAA
• Inferior MI

cards.question: Differential: s: Headache red flags
cards.answer:
• Sudden onset (thunderclap)
• Age >50 (new headache)
• Fever + meningism
• Focal neurology
• Papilloedema
• Recent head trauma

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Bowel obstruction red flags
cards.answer: Colicky pain → constant + vomiting + absolute constipation (no flatus/feces) + distension + previous surgery → URGENT surgery consult

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Acute pancreatitis severe presentation
cards.answer: Severe epigastric pain radiating to back + vomiting + alcohol/gallstones + tachycardia + hypotension → ICU if severe

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Ascending cholangitis (Charcot's triad)
cards.answer: RUQ pain + fever + jaundice → URGENT resuscitation, antibiotics, ERCP within 24-48h

cards.question: Differential: s: RLQ pain differentials
cards.answer: • Acute appendicitis • Ectopic pregnancy • Ovarian torsion • PID • Renal colic • Crohn's disease • Cecal pathology

cards.question: Differential: s: LLQ pain differentials
cards.answer: • Acute diverticulitis • Ectopic pregnancy • Ovarian torsion • PID • Renal colic • Ulcerative colitis • Colourectal cancer

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Withholding analgesia before surgical review
cards.answer: GIVE adequate analgesia - does NOT mask signs, improves patient comfort and cooperation with examination

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Missing AAA in elderly with abdominal pain
cards.answer: ALWAYS consider AAA in patients >60 with abdominal/back pain. Palpate for pulsatile mass. URGENT CT angiogram if suspected.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not recognising mesenteric ischaemia
cards.answer: 'Pain out of proportion to examination' = CRITICAL red flag. Elderly + AF + severe abdominal pain → Check lactate, URGENT CT angiogram, IMMEDIATE surgery.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Upper GI bleeding red flags (urgent endoscopy)
cards.answer: Haematemesis + hypotension (SBP <100) OR tachycardia (HR >100) OR Hb <70 → URGENT endoscopy within 24h

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Variceal bleeding management
cards.answer: Known cirrhosis + haematemesis → Terlipressin + antibiotics (ceftriaxone) + URGENT endoscopy (variceal banding) + octreotide

cards.question: Differential: s: Upper GI bleeding causes
cards.answer: • Peptic ulcer (50%) • Oesophageal varices (15%) • Mallory-Weiss tear • Gastritis/erosions • Oesophagitis • Malignancy

cards.question: Differential: s: Lower GI bleeding causes
cards.answer: • Diverticulosis • Angiodysplasia • Haemorrhoids • Anal fissure • IBD • Colourectal cancer • Ischaemic colitis

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Thunderclap headache (worst headache of life)
cards.answer: Sudden onset severe headache reaching peak <1 minute → URGENT CT head + LP if CT negative (subarachnoid haemorrhage until proven otherwise)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Headache with fever and neck stiffness
cards.answer: Headache + fever + neck stiffness + photophobia → Meningitis. URGENT LP + blood cultures + IV ceftriaxone

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Headache with focal neurology
cards.answer: Headache + focal neurology (weakness, sensory loss, visual field defect, speech disturbance) → Space-occupying lesion, stroke. URGENT CT/MRI

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Headache with papilloedema
cards.answer: Headache + papilloedema + visual obscurations → Raised ICP. URGENT CT head + LP (measure opening pressure)

cards.question: Differential: s: Primary headaches
cards.answer: • Migraine (with/without aura) • Tension-type headache • Cluster headache • Medication overuse headache

cards.question: Differential: s: Secondary headaches (life-threatening)
cards.answer: • Subarachnoid haemorrhage • Meningitis • Encephalitis • Space-occupying lesion • Temporal arteritis • Acute angle-closure glaucoma

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Peritonitis clinical features
cards.answer: Guarding (involuntary muscle spasm) + rigidity (board-like abdomen) + rebound tenderness + percussion tenderness + lying still → IMMEDIATE surgery

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Strangulated hernia
cards.answer: Irreducible tender hernia + overlying skin changes (erythema) + systemic upset (fever, tachycardia) → IMMEDIATE surgery (bowel ischaemia risk)

cards.question: Physical exam: Acute abdomen examination sequence
cards.answer: 1. Inspection (scars, distension, masses) 2. Palpation (start away from pain, assess peritonism) 3. Percussion (liver span, shifting dullness, rebound) 4. Auscultation (bowel sounds) 5. Special tests (Murphy's, McBurney's, Rovsing's)

cards.question: Physical exam: Murphy's sign (positive finding)
cards.answer: Palpate RUQ whilst patient takes deep breath → Sudden cessation of inspiration due to pain = Positive Murphy's sign → Acute cholecystitis

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Pre-eclampsia severe features
cards.answer: BP ≥160/110 + proteinuria + (severe headache OR visual disturbance OR epigastric pain OR elevated LFTs OR platelets <100) → URGENT MgSO4 + delivery

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Placental abruption
cards.answer: Constant severe abdominal pain + woody hard uterus + vaginal bleeding + fetal distress → IMMEDIATE delivery (Category 1 C-section if fetus alive)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Reduced fetal movements
cards.answer: Maternal perception of reduced fetal movements ≥28 weeks → URGENT CTG + ultrasound (up to 50% of stillbirths preceded by reduced movements)

cards.question: Differential: s: First trimester bleeding causes
cards.answer: • Miscarriage (threatened, inevitable, incomplete, complete) • Ectopic pregnancy • Molar pregnancy • Cervical causes (polyp, ectropion, cancer) • Implantation bleeding

cards.question: Differential: s: Third trimester bleeding causes
cards.answer: • Placenta praevia • Placental abruption • Vasa praevia • Show (bloody mucous plug) • Local causes (cervical, vaginal)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: High suicide risk features
cards.answer: Specific plan + means available + intent + no protective factors + previous attempts + hopelessness + psychosis with command hallucinations → Admit involuntarily if refuses

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Acute violence risk
cards.answer: Recent violence + threats + psychosis with paranoid delusions + agitation + weapons access + substance intoxication → IMMEDIATE safety measures (security, de-escalation, sedation)

cards.question: Communication: Asking about suicidal ideation
cards.answer: "Have you been feeling so low that you've had thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life?" (Direct, non-judgmental, shows concern)

cards.question: Communication: Assessing suicide plan
cards.answer: "Have you thought about how you might do it?" then "Do you have access to [means]?" and "When were you thinking of doing this?"

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Meningococcal septicaemia
cards.answer: Non-blanching purpuric rash + fever + unwell child → IMMEDIATE IM/IV benzylpenicillin + hospital transfer (DON'T delay for LP)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Febrile child <3 months
cards.answer: Any fever in infant <3 months → High risk of serious bacterial infection. Admit + full septic screen + IV antibiotics

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Respiratory distress in children
cards.answer: Grunting + nasal flaring + subcostal/intercostal recession + tracheal tug + SpO2 <92% → High-flow O2 + URGENT paediatric review

cards.question: eTG (Therapeutic Guidelines)
cards.answer: Australian evidence-based guidelines for medication and management. FREE access via NPS MedicineWise app. ALWAYS reference eTG in AMC OSCE for antibiotic choices, dosing.

cards.question: ANZCOR (resuscitation guidelines)
cards.answer: Australian and New Zealand Committee on Resuscitation. Use ANZCOR protocols for CPR, anaphylaxis (adrenaline doses), ALS algorithms.

cards.question: Community pharmacy access
cards.answer: Australian pharmacies provide emergency contraception (without prescription), nicotine replacement therapy, some antibiotics (UTI - pharmacist-only). Mention in safety-netting.

cards.question: Bulk billing and costs
cards.answer: Mention costs in counselling: 'This medication is PBS-listed, so it will cost you $XX at the pharmacy.' Shows cultural awareness of Australian healthcare system.

cards.question: spelling: Key medical terms
cards.answer: Use -ise not -ize (e.g., hospitalise, organise), -our not -or (e.g., labour, tumour), -ae not -e (e.g., paediatric, anaesthesia), -re not -er (e.g., centre, litre)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Mesenteric ischaemia pain out of proportion
cards.answer: Severe abdominal pain DISPROPORTIONATE to examination findings + elderly + AF/vascular disease → HIGH risk bowel infarction → Elevated lactate + URGENT CT angiogram + IMMEDIATE surgery

cards.question: Acute cholecystitis antibiotic choice (eTG)
cards.answer: Ceftriaxone 1g IV daily + metronidazole 500mg IV TDS (eTG 2024 first-line for acute cholecystitis)

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not doing pregnancy test in all women 15-50
cards.answer: ALWAYS βhCG in women of childbearing age (15-50) with abdominal pain, even if period recent. Ectopic can present atypically. Medicolegal risk.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Discharging 'gastroenteritis' without red flag screening
cards.answer: Before diagnosing gastroenteritis, ALWAYS exclude: AAA (elderly), mesenteric ischaemia (elderly + AF), early appendicitis, ectopic pregnancy. If ANY red flags → investigate.

cards.question: Differential: s: Central abdominal pain causes
cards.answer: • Small bowel obstruction • Gastroenteritis • Early appendicitis (before RLQ migration) • Mesenteric ischaemia • AAA • IBS (chronic)

cards.question: Differential: s: Suprapubic pain causes
cards.answer: • UTI (cystitis) • Urinary retention • PID • Ectopic pregnancy/miscarriage • Endometriosis

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not checking for peritonism systematically
cards.answer: ALWAYS examine for peritonism: Guarding, rigidity, rebound tenderness, percussion tenderness, patient lying still. Peritonitis = surgical emergency.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Tension pneumothorax clinical features
cards.answer: Tracheal deviation AWAY from affected side + hypotension + respiratory distress + distended neck veins → IMMEDIATE needle decompression (2nd intercostal space midclavicular line) before CXR

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Massive PE presentation
cards.answer: Sudden onset dyspnoea + hypotension + raised JVP + right heart strain on ECG (S1Q3T3, RBBB) → IMMEDIATE anticoagulation + thrombolysis if unstable

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Acute pulmonary oedema
cards.answer: Severe dyspnoea + pink frothy sputum + bilateral basal crackles + hypoxia → Sit upright + high-flow O2 + IV frusemide + GTN + CPAP

cards.question: Differential: s: Acute dyspnoea causes
cards.answer: • Pulmonary oedema (LVF) • Pneumonia • PE • Pneumothorax • Asthma/COPD exacerbation • Pleural effusion • Anaphylaxis

cards.question: Differential: s: Chest pain (cardiac vs non-cardiac)
cards.answer: CARDIAC: ACS, pericarditis, aortic dissection NON-CARDIAC: PE, pneumothorax, pneumonia, GORD, musculoskeletal, anxiety

cards.question: Troponin interpretation in Australia
cards.answer: High-sensitivity troponin used in Australian hospitals. Repeat at 1 hour (0/1h pathway) for ACS rule-out. Normal troponin does NOT exclude ACS if chest pain ongoing - repeat ECG.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Missing aortic dissection in chest pain
cards.answer: Sudden onset tearing chest pain radiating to back + BP difference between arms >20mmHg → Aortic dissection. URGENT CT angiogram. Do NOT give thrombolysis (fatal).

cards.question: Physical exam: Upper motor neuron vs lower motor neuron signs
cards.answer: UMN: Increased tone, brisk reflexes, upgoing plantars, no fasciculations LMN: Decreased tone, reduced/absent reflexes, downgoing plantars, muscle wasting, fasciculations

cards.question: Physical exam: MRC power grading scale
cards.answer: 0 = No movement 1 = Flicker of movement 2 = Movement with gravity eliminated 3 = Movement against gravity 4 = Movement against resistance (weak) 5 = Normal power

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Cauda equina syndrome
cards.answer: Bilateral leg weakness + saddle anaesthesia + urinary retention/incontinence + reduced anal tone → IMMEDIATE MRI spine + neurosurgical decompression <48h

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Guillain-Barré syndrome (acute ascending paralysis)
cards.answer: Ascending symmetrical weakness + areflexia + recent infection (Campylobacter, CMV) → Risk respiratory failure. Monitor FVC, admit ICU if FVC <15mL/kg. IVIg or plasmapheresis.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Myasthenia gravis crisis
cards.answer: Fluctuating weakness worse with fatigue + ptosis/diplopia + respiratory muscle weakness → Myasthenic crisis. Urgent FVC monitoring, ICU if FVC <15mL/kg, plasmapheresis.

cards.question: Differential: s: Acute limb weakness causes
cards.answer: • Stroke (UMN) • GBS (LMN) • Spinal cord compression (UMN) • Myasthenia gravis • Periodic paralysis • Functional (non-organic)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Massive haemorrhage in trauma
cards.answer: Hypotension (SBP <90) + tachycardia (HR >120) + external bleeding/suspected internal bleeding → Activate massive transfusion protocol: Blood products 1:1:1 (RBC:FFP:platelets) + tranexamic acid 1g IV + damage control surgery

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Flail chest
cards.answer: Paradoxical chest wall movement (segment moves inward on inspiration) + respiratory distress → High-flow O2 + adequate analgesia (epidural/PCA) + monitor for respiratory failure

cards.question: Physical exam: ATLS primary survey (ABCDE)
cards.answer: A = Airway + C-spine B = Breathing C = Circulation + haemorrhage control D = Disability (GCS, pupils) E = Exposure + environment control (prevent hypothermia)

cards.question: Physical exam: FAST scan in trauma
cards.answer: Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma. Rapid bedside ultrasound to detect free fluid (blood) in: 1) Pericardium 2) RUQ (hepatorenal) 3) LUQ (splenorenal) 4) Pelvis. FAST positive + unstable = immediate laparotomy.

cards.question: Trauma transfer criteria (NSW)
cards.answer: Major trauma → Transfer to Major Trauma Service (Royal Prince Alfred, Liverpool, St George, Westmead, John Hunter, Gosford). Criteria: GCS <13, penetrating injury, major burns, multi-system injury.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not maintaining C-spine immobilization
cards.answer: ASSUME cervical spine injury in ALL trauma patients until cleared clinically or radiologically. Maintain in-line immobilization, hard collar + blocks + tape, clear with NEXUS or CCR + CT if indicated.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Postmenopausal bleeding (PMB)
cards.answer: ANY vaginal bleeding >12 months after last period = endometrial cancer until proven otherwise → URGENT pelvic ultrasound (endometrial thickness) + biopsy. 10% of PMB cases are malignant.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Post-coital bleeding (PCB)
cards.answer: Bleeding after sexual intercourse = cervical pathology (cancer, polyp, ectropion) → URGENT speculum examination + cervical smear/biopsy

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Ovarian torsion
cards.answer: Sudden onset severe unilateral pelvic pain + nausea/vomiting + tender adnexal mass on examination → URGENT pelvic ultrasound (Doppler shows reduced ovarian blood flow) → URGENT laparoscopy to untwist (preserve ovary)

cards.question: Differential: s: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) causes
cards.answer: STRUCTURAL (PALM): Polyps, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma (fibroids), Malignancy NON-STRUCTURAL (COEIN): Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not classified

cards.question: Differential: s: Acute pelvic pain in women
cards.answer: GYNAE: Ectopic pregnancy, ovarian torsion, PID, ovarian cyst rupture, endometriosis NON-GYNAE: Appendicitis, UTI, renal colic, bowel obstruction

cards.question: Contraception PBS restrictions
cards.answer: Combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP): PBS-listed, cheap. Long-acting reversible contraception (LARC): Implanon NXT (PBS), Mirena IUS (PBS with restrictions). Copper IUD not PBS-listed.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not recognizing PCB as red flag
cards.answer: Post-coital bleeding is NEVER normal. Always examine cervix + refer for colposcopy if abnormal appearance. High risk of cervical cancer/pre-cancer.

cards.question: Physical exam: MSE (Mental State Examination) components
cards.answer: A = Appearance/behaviour S = Speech E = Emotion (mood) P = Perception (hallucinations) T = Thought (form, content) I = Insight C = Cognition (orientation, memory, attention)

cards.question: Physical exam: Assessing suicidal risk in MSE
cards.answer: Thought content: Active suicidal ideation? Plan? Intent? Means? Mood: Hopelessness? Severe depression? Insight: Recognizes need for help? Protective factors: Family, future plans, religious beliefs?

cards.question: Differential: s: Psychosis differential diagnosis
cards.answer: PRIMARY: Schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, delusional disorder, brief psychotic disorder SECONDARY: Drug-induced (cannabis, stimulants), medical (delirium, dementia, seizures), mood disorder with psychotic features

cards.question: Communication: Responding to delusions
cards.answer: DON'T: Challenge or agree with delusion DO: Acknowledge distress without reinforcing belief: 'I can see this is very distressing for you. I'd like to help you feel safer.'

cards.question: Mental Health Act (NSW)
cards.answer: Involuntary admission criteria: Mental illness + risk (self/others) + refuse voluntary admission + no less restrictive alternative. Requires 2 medical practitioners + Mental Health Review Tribunal review within 21 days.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Kawasaki disease
cards.answer: Fever >5 days + 4/5: (1) Bilateral conjunctivitis (2) Cervical lymphadenopathy (3) Polymorphous rash (4) Extremity changes (5) Oral changes (strawberry tongue) → Risk coronary artery aneurysms → URGENT echocardiogram + IV immunoglobulin + aspirin

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Intussusception
cards.answer: Intermittent colicky abdominal pain + vomiting + redcurrant jelly stool + palpable RUQ mass ('sausage-shaped') → URGENT ultrasound (target sign) → Air enema reduction (80% success) or surgery

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Non-accidental injury (NAI) red flags
cards.answer: Bruising in non-mobile infant, multiple bruises different ages, patterned injuries, injuries inconsistent with history, delayed presentation, fractures (ribs, metaphyseal) → NOTIFY child protection, skeletal survey, ophthalmology (retinal haemorrhages)

cards.question: Differential: s: Fever without focus in children
cards.answer: Age <3 months: Sepsis, meningitis, UTI, viral Age 3-36 months: Viral (most common), UTI, bacteraemia, pneumonia, meningitis Occult bacteraemia now rare (Hib, pneumococcal vaccines)

cards.question: Paediatric immunization schedule
cards.answer: National Immunization Program: Birth (Hep B), 2m (6-in-1 + PCV + rotavirus), 4m (same), 6m (6-in-1 + Hep B + PCV), 12m (MMR + MenACWY + PCV), 18m (6-in-1 + Hib + MenB). FREE under Medicare.

cards.question: Communication: Explaining febrile convulsion to parents
cards.answer: "Febrile convulsions are seizures triggered by fever, common in children 6 months - 5 years. They look frightening but are usually harmless and don't cause brain damage. Most children outgrow them. If it happens again, place them on their side in a safe place and time the seizure. Call ambulance if >5 minutes."

cards.question: Communication: Breaking bad news - SPIKES framework
cards.answer: S = Setting (private, sit down) P = Perception (what do you know?) I = Invitation (do you want to know?) K = Knowledge (warning shot + small chunks) E = Empathy (acknowledge emotions) S = Strategy + Summary

cards.question: Communication: Warning shot before bad news
cards.answer: "I'm afraid I have some difficult news to share with you." PAUSE. Allows patient to prepare emotionally. DON'T rush into diagnosis.

cards.question: Communication: Responding to anger
cards.answer: Acknowledge emotion: "I can see you're very angry." Allow silence. Don't take it personally or become defensive. Once emotion settles: "Tell me what's most concerning for you."

cards.question: Communication: Responding to tears/sadness
cards.answer: Offer tissue. Silence. Physical gesture if appropriate (hand on shoulder - ask permission in OSCE). "I can see this is very difficult for you. Take your time." DON'T rush to next topic.

cards.question: Interpreter services
cards.answer: Telephone Interpreter Service (TIS National): 131 450. ALWAYS use professional interpreter for non-English speakers. DO NOT use family members for medical consultations (confidentiality, accuracy issues).

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Using medical jargon without explaining
cards.answer: Say: 'CT scan - a detailed imaging test' NOT 'We need to organize a CT' Say: 'The cancer has spread' NOT 'There are metastases' Always check understanding: 'Can I check I've explained that clearly?'

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Anaphylaxis immediate management
cards.answer: Remove trigger → Lie flat + raise legs → IM adrenaline 0.5mg (0.5mL of 1:1000) anterolateral thigh → Repeat every 5 minutes if no response → High-flow O2 → IV fluids (20mL/kg bolus) → Call for help

cards.question: Anaphylaxis adrenaline dose (ANZCOR)
cards.answer: ADULT: 0.5mg (0.5mL of 1:1000) IM CHILD <5 years: 0.15mg 6-12 years: 0.3mg >12 years: 0.5mg Route: IM anterolateral thigh (NOT IV unless specialist)

cards.question: EpiPen prescription
cards.answer: After anaphylaxis: Prescribe EpiPen (adrenaline auto-injector) x2. NOT PBS-listed (expensive ~$100 each). Action plan + allergy specialist referral. Teach patient/family how to use.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Giving IV adrenaline instead of IM
cards.answer: IM adrenaline is SAFER than IV. IV adrenaline only in cardiac arrest or by specialists (risk of arrhythmia, hypertensive crisis). In OSCE: 'I would give IM adrenaline 0.5mg immediately.'

cards.question: Communication: Anaphylaxis discharge advice
cards.answer: "You've had a severe allergic reaction. Avoid [trigger]. I'm prescribing two EpiPens - carry them always. If symptoms return: Use EpiPen immediately into outer thigh, call 000, lie down. You'll need allergy specialist review to identify exact trigger and long-term plan."

cards.question: Physical exam: ECG systematic interpretation (DR ABCDEs)
cards.answer: D = Define (rate, rhythm) R = aRrhythmia A = Axis B = Blocks (AV, bundle branch) C = Chambers (hypertrophy) D = Dangerous (STEMI, hyperkalaemia, long QT) E = Everything else

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: STEMI ECG criteria
cards.answer: ST elevation ≥1mm in 2 contiguous leads (or ≥2mm in chest leads) → STEMI → Immediate aspirin 300mg + ticagrelor 180mg + morphine + antiemetic + cardiology (PCI within 90 minutes target)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Hyperkalaemia on ECG
cards.answer: Tall peaked T waves + wide QRS + loss of P waves → Severe hyperkalaemia → IMMEDIATE calcium gluconate 10mL 10% IV (stabilize membrane) + insulin-dextrose + salbutamol nebulizer (shift K+ intracellularly) + treat cause

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Long QT syndrome
cards.answer: QTc >500ms + syncope/seizures → Risk of torsades de pointes (fatal arrhythmia) → Stop QT-prolonging drugs + electrolytes (Mg2+, K+, Ca2+) + cardiology ± beta-blockers/ICD

cards.question: Differential: s: ST elevation causes
cards.answer: • STEMI (most important) • Pericarditis (widespread concave ST elevation + PR depression) • Left ventricular aneurysm (persistent ST elevation) • Benign early repolarization (young patients) • Prinzmetal angina

cards.question: Diabetes medications PBS restrictions
cards.answer: Metformin: PBS-listed (first-line) SGLT2 inhibitors: PBS requires HbA1c >7% despite metformin GLP-1 agonists: PBS requires BMI >30 + HbA1c >7% Insulin: PBS-listed Check PBS before prescribing expensive agents.

cards.question: NDSS (National Diabetes Services Scheme)
cards.answer: Free registration. Provides subsidized blood glucose monitoring equipment, insulin pump consumables, education. Register ALL diabetic patients: 'I'll arrange NDSS registration - this gives you cheaper test strips and equipment.'

cards.question: Communication: Explaining Type 2 diabetes diagnosis
cards.answer: "Your blood tests show you have Type 2 diabetes. This means your body doesn't use insulin properly, causing high blood sugar. We can manage this with diet changes, exercise, and medication. The goal is to prevent complications like heart disease, kidney disease, and vision problems. Let's make a plan together."

cards.question: Physical exam: ASA classification
cards.answer: ASA 1: Normal healthy ASA 2: Mild systemic disease ASA 3: Severe systemic disease ASA 4: Severe disease, constant threat to life ASA 5: Moribund, not expected to survive ASA 6: Brain dead organ donor

cards.question: Surgical category (Australian triage)
cards.answer: Cat 1: Life-threatening, immediate (AAA, ruptured ectopic) Cat 2: Urgent, within 30 days (cancer surgery) Cat 3: Not life-threatening, within 365 days (elective hernia, gallstones) Affects waiting times in public hospitals.

cards.question: VTE prophylaxis guidelines
cards.answer: All surgical patients: Risk-assess using ANZCA guidelines. Most patients: LMWH (enoxaparin 40mg SC daily) + TED stockings + early mobilization. Continue until mobile. High-risk: Extended prophylaxis post-discharge.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not documenting informed consent
cards.answer: Informed consent requires: (1) Diagnosis (2) Procedure details (3) Risks + benefits (4) Alternatives (5) What if decline. Document conversation in notes. Patient signs consent form. Medicolegal protection.

cards.question: Emergency contraception access
cards.answer: Levonorgestrel (Postinor, NorLevo): Available from pharmacy WITHOUT prescription (over-counter). Take within 72h of unprotected sex (earlier = more effective). Not PBS-listed (~$20-40).

cards.question: Communication: Contraception counselling framework
cards.answer: GATHER: G = Greet warmly, A = Ask about patient, T = Tell about options, H = Help choose, E = Explain how to use, R = Return visit

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not screening for COCP contraindications
cards.answer: WHO Category 4 (absolute contraindications): Migraine with aura, VTE history, breast cancer, <6 weeks postpartum + breastfeeding, smoker >35 years (>15 cig/day), uncontrolled hypertension. ALWAYS screen before prescribing.

cards.question: Physical exam: Capacity assessment (4 components)
cards.answer: 1. UNDERSTAND relevant information 2. RETAIN information (doesn't need to be long-term) 3. USE AND WEIGH information (reasoning process) 4. COMMUNICATE decision Lacks capacity if fails ANY component.

cards.question: Guardianship Tribunal (NSW)
cards.answer: If patient lacks capacity for medical decisions + no Enduring Guardian appointed → Apply to NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT) for guardian appointment. Emergency medical treatment can proceed without consent if in best interests.

cards.question: Communication: Assessing capacity - USE AND WEIGH
cards.answer: "What are the benefits of [treatment]?" "What are the risks?" "What might happen if you don't have this treatment?" "Why have you decided to [accept/refuse]?" Assesses reasoning, not just recall.

cards.question: Physical exam: Developmental domains (4 areas)
cards.answer: 1. GROSS MOTOR (sitting, walking, running) 2. FINE MOTOR + VISION (grasp, drawing, building) 3. SPEECH + HEARING (babbling, words, sentences) 4. SOCIAL + EMOTIONAL (smiling, playing, self-care)

cards.question: Physical exam: Red flags for developmental delay
cards.answer: 6 months: Not smiling, no head control 12 months: Not sitting, no babbling, no response to name 18 months: Not walking, no words 2 years: Not running, <10 words, not combining words Any loss of skills = URGENT referral

cards.question: Communication: Discussing developmental concerns with parents
cards.answer: "I've noticed [specific concern] during today's check. This might be normal variation, but I'd like to refer to a paediatrician to make sure we're not missing anything. Early assessment means we can provide support if needed." Avoid alarmist language.

cards.question: Communication: Cultural sensitivity in bad news
cards.answer: ASK about preferences: "Some people want all the details, others prefer family to know first. What would you prefer?" Respect family involvement (common in many cultures) Use professional interpreters Avoid assumptions about religion/culture

cards.question: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health
cards.answer: Close the Gap initiative. Higher rates of chronic disease (diabetes, renal, cardiovascular). Ask: "Do you identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander?" (health records, access to specific programs). Respect cultural practices, involve Aboriginal Health Workers.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Direct bad news delivery without preparation
cards.answer: DON'T: "Your scan shows cancer." DO: Warning shot + pause → "I'm afraid I have some difficult news." PAUSE. "The scan shows an abnormality that looks like cancer." PAUSE. Check understanding, allow emotions.

cards.question: Medicare and specialist referrals
cards.answer: GP referral required for specialist appointments to claim Medicare rebate. Referral valid 12 months (3 months for some specialists). Mention in OSCE: 'I'll write a referral letter for you to see the specialist, which means you can claim a Medicare rebate.'

cards.question: PBS Safety Net
cards.answer: After spending threshold on PBS medications in a year, further PBS medications cheaper (Safety Net price). Mention to patients with multiple medications: 'Keep your pharmacy receipts - you might reach the Safety Net threshold.'

cards.question: After-hours GP services
cards.answer: After-hours GP clinics (evenings/weekends), Home Doctor service (bulk-billed home visits), 13HEALTH (13 43 25 84) nurse advice line. Mention in safety-netting: 'If you're concerned tonight, you can call 13HEALTH or attend after-hours GP.'

cards.question: Communication: Safety-netting (red flags for patients)
cards.answer: ALWAYS give specific red flags: "Return to ED or call 000 if you develop: [specific symptoms relevant to diagnosis - e.g., severe headache, fever, vomiting, rash, confusion]." NOT just 'come back if worse.'

cards.question: Communication: Shared decision-making
cards.answer: Present options + risks/benefits → Explore patient values/preferences → Make recommendation but respect patient autonomy → 'What's most important to you?' DON'T dictate, DON'T leave patient without guidance.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not addressing patient's health litreacy
cards.answer: Use Teach-Back method: 'I want to make sure I've explained this clearly. Can you tell me in your own words what you'll do when you get home?' Identifies misunderstandings. Write down key points.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Inadequate pain management
cards.answer: Australian guidelines: WHO pain ladder. Paracetamol 1g QID (max 4g/day) + ibuprofen 400mg TDS (if no contraindications) + opioid if severe. DON'T under-treat pain. Monitor for adverse effects (constipation with opioids).

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Sepsis recognition (qSOFA)
cards.answer: Quick SOFA: RR ≥22, altered mentation (GCS <15), SBP ≤100 → Suspect sepsis → Sepsis 6 (within 1 hour): Take 3 (cultures, lactate, FBC) + Give 3 (O2, IV fluids, IV antibiotics)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Hypoglycaemia management
cards.answer: BGL <4mmol/L + symptoms OR BGL <3mmol/L → Conscious: 15g rapid-acting carbs (jelly beans, juice) → Recheck BGL in 15 min → Unconscious: IM glucagon 1mg OR IV glucose 10% 150mL

cards.question: Differential: s: Confusion/delirium causes (surgical patients)
cards.answer: Common post-op causes: Hypoxia, infection (pneumonia, UTI), medications (opioids, benzodiazepines), metabolic (hypoglycaemia, electrolytes), alcohol withdrawal, urinary retention, pain, constipation

cards.question: Differential: s: Collapse/syncope causes
cards.answer: CARDIAC: Arrhythmia, AS, PE, MI NEUROLOGICAL: Seizure, TIA/stroke VASOVAGAL: Most common, benign OTHER: Hypoglycaemia, postural hypotension, medications

cards.question: Physical exam: Fundoscopy - hypertensive retinopathy grading
cards.answer: Grade 1: Silver wiring Grade 2: AV nipping Grade 3: Flame haemorrhages + cotton wool spots Grade 4: Papilloedema (hypertensive emergency)

cards.question: Physical exam: Respiratory examination - percussion notes
cards.answer: Resonant: Normal lung Hyperresonant: Pneumothorax, emphysema Dull: Consolidation, pleural effusion, lung collapse Stony dull: Large pleural effusion

cards.question: Notifiable diseases (NSW)
cards.answer: Immediately notifiable (phone): Measles, viral haemorrhagic fever, diphtheria, polio, rabies, plague, anthrax 48-hour notification: TB, HIV, hepatitis B/C, pertussis, meningococcal, invasive pneumococcal Notify NSW Health Protection Unit

cards.question: Workplace injury (WorkCover NSW)
cards.answer: Workplace injury → WorkCover claim. Doctor provides medical certificate. Treatment costs covered by WorkCover (not Medicare/PBS). Patient needs employer details for claim. Doctor completes Certificate of Capacity for return to work.

cards.question: Medical certificates (sick leave)
cards.answer: Standard certificate: Date, patient name, fitness for work (unfit/suitable for modified duties), period, doctor signature. DON'T disclose diagnosis without consent. 'Unable to attend work due to medical reasons' is sufficient.

cards.question: Communication: Breaking bad news to non-English speaker
cards.answer: ALWAYS use professional interpreter (TIS: 131 450). Brief interpreter beforehand. Speak directly to patient (not interpreter). Use short sentences. Pause for interpretation. Check understanding via interpreter.

cards.question: Communication: Obtaining consent for procedure
cards.answer: Explain: (1) What will be done (2) Why needed (3) Risks/benefits (4) Alternatives (5) What if decline. Check understanding: 'What questions do you have?' Confirm: 'Do you agree to proceed?' Document.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not exploring patient's ICE (Ideas, Concerns, Expectations)
cards.answer: Early in consultation ask: 'What were you thinking might be causing this?' (Ideas) 'Is there anything particular that's worrying you?' (Concerns) 'What were you hoping we might do today?' (Expectations). Improves satisfaction.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Closing consultation abruptly
cards.answer: Always: (1) Summarize (2) Check understanding (3) Safety-net (when to return) (4) Follow-up plan (5) 'Any other questions?' (6) Provide written information if appropriate. Never rush the ending.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Massive haematemesis immediate management
cards.answer: Haematemesis + haemodynamic instability → 2x large-bore IV (14-16G) + crossmatch 6 units + IV tranexamic acid 1g + activate massive transfusion + URGENT endoscopy + ICU

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of melaena (black tarry stool)
cards.answer:
• Peptic ulcer (most common)
• Oesophageal varices
• Mallory-Weiss tear
• Gastritis
• Upper GI malignancy
• Aorto-enteric fistula (if AAA repair history)

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not calculating Rockall score in upper GI bleed
cards.answer: Rockall score predicts rebleeding and mortality. Age, shock, comorbidities, diagnosis, stigmata of recent haemorrhage. Score ≥3 = high risk → URGENT endoscopy.

cards.question: Upper GI endoscopy timing (eTG guidelines)
cards.answer:
HIGH RISK (Rockall ≥3, ongoing bleeding, hypotension): Endoscopy within 24h
AVERAGE RISK: Endoscopy within 24-48h
LOW RISK: Outpatient endoscopy
All receive IV PPI (pantoprazole 80mg bolus + 8mg/h infusion)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Cardiac tamponade (Beck's triad)
cards.answer: Hypotension + raised JVP + muffled heart sounds + pulsus paradoxus → URGENT pericardiocentesis (echo-guided)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Acute severe asthma (life-threatening features)
cards.answer: Silent chest + cyanosis + exhaustion + confusion + bradycardia + hypotension → Immediate high-flow O2 + salbutamol continuous nebulizer + IV magnesium + hydrocortisone + ICU

cards.question: Differential: s: Chronic cough causes (>8 weeks)
cards.answer:
• Post-nasal drip (upper airway cough syndrome)
• Asthma/eosinophilic bronchitis
• GORD
• ACE inhibitor
• Chronic bronchitis
• Bronchiectasis
• Lung cancer

cards.question: Physical exam: Differentiating pleural effusion vs consolidation
cards.answer:
EFFUSION: Stony dull percussion + reduced breath sounds + reduced vocal resonance
CONSOLIDATION: Dull percussion + bronchial breathing + increased vocal resonance + crackles

cards.question: Oxygen prescribing in COPD
cards.answer: Target SpO2 88-92% in COPD (not 94-98%). Risk of CO2 retention with high-flow O2 → Venturi mask (fixed concentration): 24%, 28% initially. Monitor ABG.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Bacterial meningitis empirical treatment
cards.answer:
Suspected meningitis + NO focal neurology/papilloedema → LP + blood cultures → IV ceftriaxone 2g BD (+ ampicillin if >50 years for Listeria) + dexamethasone 10mg QID x 4 days
If focal neurology/papilloedema → CT first, then LP

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of headache + fever
cards.answer:
• Meningitis (bacterial, viral, fungal)
• Encephalitis
• Brain abscess
• Sinusitis
• Viral illness (influenza)
• Malaria (if returned traveler)

cards.question: Physical exam: Kernig's sign vs Brudzinski's sign
cards.answer:
KERNIG'S: Hip flexed to 90°, attempt to extend knee → Pain/resistance = positive (meningism)
BRUDZINSKI'S: Passive neck flexion → Involuntary hip/knee flexion = positive (meningism)

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Giving steroids before LP in suspected meningitis
cards.answer: Give dexamethasone AFTER or WITH first dose of antibiotics (NOT before). If delay in LP, give antibiotics immediately, don't wait for LP. DON'T delay antibiotics for imaging.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Stroke thrombolysis timeframe
cards.answer: Ischaemic stroke + <4.5 hours from onset + no contraindications (haemorrhage on CT, recent surgery, bleeding disorder, BP >185/110) → IV alteplase 0.9mg/kg + thrombectomy if large vessel occlusion

cards.question: Physical exam: FAST (stroke recognition)
cards.answer:
F = Face (facial droop)
A = Arms (arm drift)
S = Speech (slurred, unable to speak)
T = Time (call 000 immediately)
Positive FAST → Stroke until proven otherwise

cards.question: Differential: s: Acute unilateral weakness causes
cards.answer:
• Stroke (most common)
• Todd's paresis (post-ictal)
• Hemiplegic migraine
• Hypoglycaemia
• Functional (conversion disorder)
• Subdural haematoma
• Brain tumor

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury
cards.answer: Myalgia + dark urine (tea-coloured) + elevated CK (>5x normal) + AKI → IV fluids (target urine output 200-300mL/h) + urinary alkalinization + monitor K+ (hyperkalaemia risk) + dialysis if severe

cards.question: Snake bite management (Australian snakes)
cards.answer: Pressure immobilization bandage + limb splint + keep still + DO NOT wash bite site → ID snake (brown, tiger, taipan, death adder, black) → Venom detection kit → Antivenom (specific to snake type) IV in monitored setting

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Status epilepticus treatment protocol
cards.answer:
Seizure >5 min or ≥2 seizures without recovery:
0-5 min: ABCDE, glucose, thiamine
5-10 min: Midazolam 10mg IM/buccal OR diazepam 10mg IV
10-20 min: Repeat benzodiazepine
20-40 min: Phenytoin 20mg/kg IV infusion OR levetiracetam
>40 min: Intubate + general anaesthesia

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of seizures (first presentation)
cards.answer:
• Idiopathic epilepsy
• Structural (stroke, tumor, head injury)
• Metabolic (hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, hypocalcaemia)
• Infection (meningitis, encephalitis)
• Drug-related (alcohol withdrawal, cocaine)
• Eclampsia (pregnant women)

cards.question: Seizure driving restrictions (NSW)
cards.answer:
First seizure: 6 months off driving (private vehicle)
Established epilepsy: 12 months seizure-free (or only sleep seizures for ≥1 year)
Commercial vehicle: 5-10 years seizure-free
Doctor MUST advise patient (document in notes)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: DKA diagnostic criteria
cards.answer:
Glucose >11mmol/L + pH <7.3 (or HCO3 <15) + ketonaemia (blood ketones >3mmol/L) or ketonuria (2+ on dipstick)
Management: IV fluids (1L 0.9% NaCl first hour) + fixed-rate insulin infusion 0.1 unit/kg/h + potassium replacement + find precipitant

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (HHS)
cards.answer: Glucose >30mmol/L + osmolality >320 + NO significant ketones + hypovolaemia → Slower rehydration than DKA (avoid cerebral oedema) + lower insulin dose + monitor Na+ closely

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of hypoglycaemia
cards.answer:
DIABETIC: Insulin/sulphonylurea excess, missed meal, exercise, alcohol
NON-DIABETIC: Insulinoma, adrenal insufficiency, liver failure, sepsis, alcohol, drugs (beta-blockers, quinine)

cards.question: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) PBS access
cards.answer: FreeStyle Libre (CGM sensor): PBS-subsidized for Type 1 diabetes (<21 years), pregnant with Type 1, or NDSS-registered Type 1 with recent severe hypo/DKA. Expensive if not eligible (~$100/sensor, lasts 14 days).

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not checking for DKA in hyperglycaemia
cards.answer: Glucose >15mmol/L → ALWAYS check ketones (blood or urine). Don't assume Type 2 diabetes can't get DKA (can occur in SGLT2 inhibitor use - 'euglycaemic DKA').

cards.question: Physical exam: Otoscopy - normal tympanic membrane landmarks
cards.answer:
Pearly grey, translucent membrane
Light reflex (5 o'clock right ear, 7 o'clock left ear)
Handle of malleus visible
Cone of light
No bulging, retraction, or perforation

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Acute epiglottitis
cards.answer: Severe sore throat + drooling + muffled voice + sitting forward (tripod position) + stridor → DO NOT examine throat (may precipitate total airway obstruction) → IMMEDIATE ENT/anaesthetics → Intubation in theatre + IV ceftriaxone

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of vertigo
cards.answer:
PERIPHERAL: BPPV (most common), vestibular neuronitis, Meniere's disease, vestibular migraine
CENTRAL: Stroke (brainstem/cerebellum), MS, tumor, medications

cards.question: Physical exam: Dix-Hallpike test (BPPV diagnosis)
cards.answer:
Patient sitting → Turn head 45° to affected side → Rapidly lie back (head hangs 20° below horizontal) → Observe for nystagmus + vertigo (latency 5-10s, fatigable) = Positive
Positive → Epley maneuver treatment

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not differentiating peripheral vs central vertigo
cards.answer:
PERIPHERAL: Horizontal/rotatory nystagmus, +ve Dix-Hallpike, NO focal neurology
CENTRAL: Vertical nystagmus, focal neurology (ataxia, diplopia, weakness) → URGENT imaging (stroke risk)

cards.question: Physical exam: ECG - STEMI territory localization
cards.answer:
ANTERIOR: V1-V4 (LAD occlusion)
INFERIOR: II, III, aVF (RCA occlusion)
LATERAL: I, aVL, V5-V6 (circumflex occlusion)
POSTERIOR: Tall R waves V1-V2 + ST depression (posterior leads V7-V9 show ST elevation)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Wellens' syndrome (LAD occlusion warning)
cards.answer: Biphasic or deeply inverted T waves in V2-V3 + recent chest pain (now pain-free) + normal/minimally elevated troponin → High risk of LAD occlusion → URGENT angiography (even if pain resolved)

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of atrial fibrillation
cards.answer:
Cardiac: IHD, valvular (mitral), heart failure, pericarditis
Non-cardiac: Hyperthyroidism, alcohol, sepsis, PE, post-operative
Lone AF (no identifiable cause)

cards.question: CHADS-VASc score for AF anticoagulation
cards.answer:
C = CHF (1), H = Hypertension (1), A = Age ≥75 (2), D = Diabetes (1), S = Stroke/TIA (2), V = Vascular disease (1), A = Age 65-74 (1), Sc = Sex female (1)
Score ≥2 men/≥3 women → Anticoagulation (apixaban, rivaroxaban, warfarin)
PBS restricts NOACs to CHADS-VASc ≥1

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not recognizing posterior MI
cards.answer: ST depression in V1-V3 in context of chest pain = posterior STEMI (NOT NSTEMI). Request posterior leads (V7-V9) showing ST elevation → Immediate PCI.

cards.question: Physical exam: Abdominal examination - McBurney's point
cards.answer: Location: 1/3 distance from ASIS to umbilicus (right lower quadrant). Maximum tenderness at McBurney's point = appendicitis (not specific, but suggestive).

cards.question: Physical exam: Rovsing's sign
cards.answer: Palpate LEFT lower quadrant → Pain in RIGHT lower quadrant = Positive Rovsing's sign → Suggests appendicitis (peritoneal irritation)

cards.question: Physical exam: Psoas sign
cards.answer: Passive right hip extension (patient lying on left side) → Pain = Positive psoas sign → Inflamed appendix overlying psoas muscle

cards.question: Physical exam: Obturator sign
cards.answer: Passive internal rotation of flexed right hip → Pain = Positive obturator sign → Inflamed appendix overlying obturator internus

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of bowel obstruction
cards.answer:
SMALL BOWEL: Adhesions (60% - previous surgery), hernias, malignancy, Crohn's, intussusception
LARGE BOWEL: Malignancy (60%), diverticular stricture, volvulus, faecal impaction

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Closed loop obstruction
cards.answer: Bowel obstruction + two points of obstruction (e.g., competent ileocaecal valve in large bowel obstruction) → Rapid distension → Perforation risk → IMMEDIATE surgery (don't wait for conservative management)

cards.question: Surgical consent documentation
cards.answer: Document in notes: Diagnosis, procedure, risks (common + serious), benefits, alternatives, patient questions, patient understanding. Patient signs consent form. For high-risk procedures, consultant should obtain consent (not junior doctor).

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not recognizing post-operative ileus
cards.answer: Post-op: No bowel sounds + distension + nausea/vomiting + no flatus → Ileus (normal after abdominal surgery, usually resolves 3-5 days). If persists >5 days or worsening → CT (exclude mechanical obstruction).

cards.question: Physical exam: Examining a lump - 7 characteristics
cards.answer:
1. Site + size
2. Shape (regular/irregular)
3. Surface (smooth/irregular)
4. Consistency (soft/firm/hard)
5. Temperature (warm = infection/inflammation)
6. Tenderness
7. Mobility (skin/muscle/fixed)

cards.question: Physical exam: Transillumination test
cards.answer: Shine light through lump in dark room. Transilluminates (light passes through) → Fluid-filled (cyst, hydrocele). Does NOT transilluminate → Solid mass.

cards.question: Differential: s: Groin lump differentials
cards.answer:
• Inguinal hernia (most common)
• Femoral hernia
• Lymph node (lymphadenopathy)
• Saphena varix
• Lipoma
• Undescended/ectopic testis
• Psoas abscess

cards.question: Physical exam: Inguinal vs femoral hernia differentiation
cards.answer:
INGUINAL: Above and medial to pubic tubercle, descends into scrotum (indirect), more common in men
FEMORAL: Below and lateral to pubic tubercle, does NOT enter scrotum, higher strangulation risk, more common in women

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Missing breast cancer red flags
cards.answer: RED FLAGS: Hard irregular lump, skin tethering, nipple inversion/retraction, peau d'orange (skin dimpling), bloody nipple discharge, axillary lymphadenopathy, age >40 → URGENT referral (2-week rule) + triple assessment (clinical + imaging + biopsy)

cards.question: Physical exam: Log roll examination technique
cards.answer: Minimum 3 people (1 controls C-spine, 2 roll patient). Maintain in-line spinal immobilization. Examine: Back, spine palpation (tenderness, step deformity), PR exam (tone, blood, prostate position). Roll back carefully.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Pelvic fracture with haemodynamic instability
cards.answer: High-impact trauma + pelvic fracture on XR + hypotension → Massive retroperitoneal haemorrhage → Pelvic binder + IV resuscitation + tranexamic acid + crossmatch 6 units + interventional radiology (embolization) OR ex-fix OR surgery

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of shock in trauma
cards.answer:
• Haemorrhagic (most common - external bleeding, internal bleeding)
• Tension pneumothorax
• Cardiac tamponade
• Neurogenic (spinal cord injury - bradycardia + hypotension)
• Septic (rare acutely)

cards.question: Major trauma criteria (NSW)
cards.answer:
HIGH RISK MECHANISM: Fall >3m, high-speed MVC, pedestrian/cyclist vs car, ejection from vehicle
PHYSIOLOGY: GCS <13, RR <10 or >29, SBP <90, penetrating injury head/neck/torso
ANATOMY: Flail chest, 2+ long bone fractures, pelvic fracture, paralysis
→ Activate trauma team

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy management
cards.answer:
Ectopic pregnancy + haemodynamic instability (hypotension, tachycardia) → Ruptured → 2x large bore IV + crossmatch + tranexamic acid + IMMEDIATE laparoscopy (salpingectomy) + resuscitation
Stable → Laparoscopy OR medical (methotrexate if criteria met)

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of miscarriage (pregnancy loss <20 weeks)
cards.answer:
• Chromosomal abnormalities (50%)
• Maternal factors (uterine anomalies, cervical incompetence, antiphospholipid syndrome)
• Infections (rare)
• Idiopathic (often no cause found)

cards.question: Physical exam: Obstetric abdominal palpation - Leopold's maneuvers
cards.answer:
1st: Fundal palpation (head vs breech)
2nd: Lateral palpation (fetal back vs limbs)
3rd: Suprapubic palpation (presenting part)
4th: Pelvic grip (engagement - 5/5 to 0/5 fifths palpable)

cards.question: Antenatal screening (public system)
cards.answer:
First trimester: Dating scan (8-12 weeks), combined first trimester screening (CFTS at 11-13 weeks - NT + βhCG + PAPP-A)
Second trimester: Morphology scan (18-20 weeks - structural abnormalities)
Gestational diabetes screening: OGTT at 24-28 weeks
All FREE in public system

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not recognizing placenta praevia risk factors
cards.answer:
RISK: Previous C-section, multiparity, advanced maternal age, smoking, previous placenta praevia
Presentation: Painless PV bleeding in 3rd trimester
Management: NO vaginal examination (precipitate massive haemorrhage), ultrasound, elective C-section at 36-37 weeks

cards.question: Physical exam: Speculum examination steps
cards.answer:
1. Consent + chaperone
2. Empty bladder
3. Lithotomy position
4. Warm speculum, lubricate with water only (not gel - interferes with cytology)
5. Insert obliquely, rotate 90°, open blades, visualize cervix
6. Cervical smear if indicated
7. Remove, rotate back

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Cervical cancer clinical features
cards.answer: Post-coital bleeding + intermenstrual bleeding + postmenopausal bleeding + foul-smelling discharge → Speculum shows abnormal cervix (ulcerated, irregular, bleeds on contact) → URGENT gynae referral + cervical biopsy

cards.question: National Cervical Screening Program
cards.answer: Cervical screening test (CST): Every 5 years from age 25-74 (changed from 2-yearly Pap smear in 2017). Tests for high-risk HPV. If HPV positive → Reflex LBC (liquid-based cytology). Self-collection option available.

cards.question: Communication: Explaining Mirena (hormonal IUS) to patient
cards.answer: "Mirena is a small T-shaped device inserted into your uterus. It releases a hormone that thins the uterine lining, reducing bleeding. It lasts 5 years, very effective contraception (>99%). Common side effects: Irregular bleeding first 3-6 months (usually settles), some women's periods stop completely (this is safe). You can have it removed anytime."

cards.question: Physical exam: Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scoring
cards.answer:
30 points total:
Orientation (10): Time 5, place 5
Registration (3): Repeat 3 words
Attention (5): Serial 7s or spell WORLD backwards
Recall (3): Recall 3 words
Language (9): Naming, repetition, 3-stage command, read, write, copy
<24/30 = cognitive impairment

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of delirium (acute confusion)
cards.answer:
DELIRIUM mnemonic:
D = Drugs (opioids, benzos, anticholinergics)
E = Eyes, ears (sensory impairment)
L = Low O2 (hypoxia, PE, MI)
I = Infection (UTI, pneumonia)
R = Retention (urinary, constipation)
I = Ictal (seizure)
U = Underhydration/undernourishment
M = Metabolic (hypoglycaemia, electrolytes)

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Lithium toxicity
cards.answer: Lithium level >1.5mmol/L + coarse tremor + ataxia + confusion + seizures + arrhythmias → STOP lithium + IV fluids + haemodialysis if severe (>2.5mmol/L) + monitor renal function + ECG

cards.question: Mental Health Treatment Plan (MHTP)
cards.answer: GP Mental Health Treatment Plan: Allows 10 subsidized psychology sessions/year (6 initial + 4 additional with review). Patient pays gap (~$50-100/session after Medicare rebate). Review required for additional sessions.

cards.question: Communication: De-escalation techniques for agitated patient
cards.answer:
1. Ensure safety (exit route, alarm)
2. Non-threatening posture (sit if safe, arms open)
3. Calm tone, slow speech
4. Active listening, validate feelings
5. Offer choices, avoid confrontation
6. Set clear limits if needed
7. Call security if unsafe

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not documenting capacity assessment properly
cards.answer: Document: (1) Decision being made (2) Information provided (3) Patient's understanding, retention, use/weigh, communication (4) Conclusion (has/lacks capacity) (5) Best interests if lacks capacity. Medicolegal protection.

cards.question: 🚨 RED FLAG: Sepsis in children (warning signs)
cards.answer: Tachycardia (age-dependent) + tachypnoea + prolonged capillary refill >2sec + reduced consciousness + mottled/pale skin + not feeding → Sepsis → IV/IO access + fluid bolus 20mL/kg + IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone) + URGENT paediatric review

cards.question: Physical exam: Assessing dehydration in children (clinical signs)
cards.answer:
MILD (3-5%): Dry mucous membranes, decreased urine output
MODERATE (5-10%): Sunken eyes, reduced skin turgor, sunken fontanelle (infants), lethargy
SEVERE (>10%): Prolonged capillary refill, tachycardia, hypotension, reduced consciousness → Shock

cards.question: Differential: s: Causes of croup vs epiglottitis vs bacterial tracheitis
cards.answer:
CROUP: Viral, barking cough, stridor, mild fever, gradual onset, age 6m-3y → Dexamethasone
EPIGLOTTITIS: Bacterial (Hib), drooling, tripod position, high fever, toxic, EMERGENCY
BACTERIAL TRACHEITIS: Post-viral, high fever, toxic, stridor, thick secretions → Intubation + antibiotics

cards.question: Paediatric early warning tool (PEWS)
cards.answer: Colour-coded observation chart in Australian hospitals (GREEN = normal, YELLOW = concerning, RED = critical). Triggers escalation to MET (Medical Emergency Team) if deteriorating. Parameters: HR, RR, work of breathing, SpO2, consciousness, temperature.

cards.question: Communication: Explaining vaccination to hesitant parents
cards.answer: "I understand you have concerns. Vaccines are very safe - tested extensively. The diseases they prevent (measles, whooping cough) can be very serious, even fatal. Side effects are usually mild (sore arm, low fever). The evidence shows vaccines don't cause autism. I recommend following the schedule to protect your child. What specific concerns do you have?"

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Not recognizing bronchiolitis severity
cards.answer: Bronchiolitis (RSV) in infant: Mild = feeding well, minimal recession → Home. SEVERE = SpO2 <92%, apnoeas, poor feeding (<50% normal), moderate-severe recession, age <3 months → ADMIT (high-flow O2, NG feeds, monitoring)

cards.question: Physical exam: Developmental milestones - 6 months
cards.answer:
GROSS MOTOR: Sits with support
FINE MOTOR: Reaches for objects, transfers hand-to-hand
SPEECH: Babbles (ba, da), responds to name
SOCIAL: Smiles responsively, stranger awareness emerging

cards.question: Physical exam: Developmental milestones - 12 months
cards.answer:
GROSS MOTOR: Pulls to stand, cruises (walks holding furniture)
FINE MOTOR: Pincer grip, puts objects in container
SPEECH: 2-3 words with meaning (mama, dada)
SOCIAL: Waves bye-bye, plays peek-a-boo

cards.question: Physical exam: Developmental milestones - 2 years
cards.answer:
GROSS MOTOR: Runs, kicks ball, walks up stairs (2 feet per step)
FINE MOTOR: Tower of 6 blocks, circular scribble
SPEECH: 50 words, 2-word sentences

cards.question: Communication: Responding to 'How long do I have?' (palliative)
cards.answer: "That's a very important question. It's difficult to give an exact timeframe - everyone is different. Based on your situation, we're thinking weeks to months rather than years. What's most important is that we focus on your comfort and quality of life. What matters most to you in the time you have?"

cards.question: Communication: Discussing DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) orders
cards.answer: "If your heart stops or you stop breathing, we can try to restart your heart with CPR (chest compressions, electric shocks). However, given your illness, CPR is unlikely to work and could cause harm (broken ribs, brain damage). I recommend focusing on comfort rather than CPR. This means natural death when it comes. What are your thoughts?"

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Breaking bad news without warning shot
cards.answer:
WRONG: "Your scan shows cancer."
RIGHT: "I'm afraid I have some difficult news." PAUSE. Check patient ready. "The scan shows..." Small chunks, check understanding.

cards.question: Communication: Responding to denial after bad news
cards.answer: "I can see this news is very difficult to accept." Don't force acceptance immediately. Allow time. Later: "I know this is hard. When you're ready, I'd like to talk about next steps." Offer support, follow-up appointment.

cards.question: Advance Care Directives (ACD) in NSW
cards.answer: Legal document where competent person states future treatment preferences. Must be in writing, signed, witnessed. Becomes active when person loses capacity. Binding on doctors (except emergency life-saving treatment). Different laws each state - NSW has Advance Care Planning framework.

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Using family as interpreters
cards.answer: NEVER use family members as interpreters for medical consultations: Confidentiality issues, inaccurate translation, family may filter/change information. ALWAYS use professional interpreters (TIS: 131 450) - telephone or in-person.

cards.question: Communication: OSCE opening (general framework)
cards.answer:
1. Greet + introduce self + role
2. Confirm patient identity
3. Explain purpose of consultation
4. Gain consent
5. Ensure privacy/comfort
6. Open question: 'What brings you in today?' or 'How can I help?'

cards.question: Communication: OSCE closing (general framework)
cards.answer:
1. Summarize key points
2. Check patient understanding: 'Can I check I've explained clearly?'
3. Address concerns: 'Any questions or worries?'
4. Safety-netting: 'Return if [specific red flags]'
5. Follow-up plan: 'I'll arrange...'
6. Thank patient

cards.question: IMG Mistake: Poor time management in OSCE
cards.answer: 8-minute OSCE = ~6 min task + 2 min closing/questions. Keep eye on clock. If running over: Summarize quickly, don't skip closing. Practice timed stations. Know when to stop gathering history and move to explanation/plan.

Not examining from BEHIND for cervical nodes: Examining cervical lymph nodes from in front of the patient is incorrect technique. You must stand behind the patient and use both hands simultaneously. This allows proper bimanual palpation and comparison of both sides. Examining from the front makes it difficult to palpate posterior chain and occipital nodes.

cards.question: What to avoid:
cards.answer: Skipping supraclavicular examination: This is a CRITICAL error. Supraclavicular nodes are often pathological, especially Virchow's node (left supraclavicular) which indicates intra-abdominal malignancy. You MUST specifically examine the supraclavicular fossa by hooking fingers over the clavicle. Ask patient to take a deep breath (makes nodes more prominent). Never skip this step.
